screen: Hero, Kanakadhara frontage, robot and parked van
text: Streets are harder than laboratories. A parked van can hide a pedestrian, and a robot that simply keeps walking can make the wrong decision. This is STREETWISE.
We recreated a street in Chennai, India.
At first, the robot just keeps walking. A person steps out from behind the van, and the robot bumps into them.
screen: Recorded robot bumps into a person
Same seed after RL; replay completion
text: Now replay the same encounter with trained navigation. PPO has learned when to slow down and wait before proceeding. The walking policy itself stays frozen. Every robot joint you see comes from recorded MuJoCo physics.

screen: Actual W&B learning graph and held-out comparison
text: These are the original training results from Weights and Biases. Across sixty-four pedestrian tests, successful crossings rose from forty-two to sixty-four. The robot also learned to give people more space.

screen: Moving-car before/after, then recorded wet-road encounter
text: Training on a molab Blackwell GPU adds lateral movement, moving cars and road defects. Mixed-hazard completion rises from twenty-eight to sixty-four out of sixty-four. Rain changes ground friction; fog limits tracking range. The first weather test still has one failure.

A separate world-model lab predicts futures and learns from simulated experience, with Weave tracing its analyst. For robot training, a challenge ladder introduces harder conditions after two perfect validation checks. Test results never control advancement.

screen: Actual native MuJoCo screenshot, simple architecture
text: Compare both policies side by side, or run live MuJoCo with Chennai geometry. Marimo, checkpoints, official SDK evidence and startup instructions make the results inspectable.
This is simulation, not a physical robot safety claim. STREETWISE helps teams discover navigation mistakes before street deployment. Robots that learn the street before they enter it.
